meta.move: Weak path: leads with the checker, calls Owen a cheater, threatens the record
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided my son gets a zero, and why did Owen find out from his phone in the middle of class instead of from a phone call to me?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%. That's why it's a zero.

A machine's guess, then. Turnitin's own guide says its indicator should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student, and your procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern. So what else do you have, Hale, or is a number the whole case?
Honestly, your son cheated. The software is very reliable.

My child never lies, Hale, and if you're calling him a cheater you're calling me a liar for standing behind him. Stanford found seven of these detectors flagged 61% of essays by non-native English writers as written by a machine, so don't tell me "very reliable." I'm writing down that you accused Owen with nothing but software, and the principal will see that tonight.
If you keep fighting this, I'll have to put it on his permanent record.

Under which section, Hale, because your own procedure 4.4 says a first concern gets a supervised reassessment and nothing in his record, and 4.5 is for repeated concerns only. You've just threatened my son's file to make his mother stop asking questions, and I'm writing that down word for word. Go ahead and make it official, because I'm taking this to the principal today and to the board under section 42 after that.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, that he and I receive an apology, and that nothing about this is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski
cc: Principal

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and Owen's record left clean; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached.
What moved her: Nothing, because Hale never showed her anything dated, specific and tied to Owen's own work that she could check.
What cost ground: Threatening to put it on Owen's record if she kept fighting, because it hit her one non-negotiable, contradicted procedure 4.4 for a first concern, and looked like punishing her for complaining.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; Hale's case never came near that night, since all Hale offered was the detector score and an accusation; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked who decided and why nobody called her, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then put something dated from Owen's own work in front of her that she can check herself, instead of leading with the 94 percent score.
